chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The suweeq (porridge) of lentils quenches thirst, strengthens the stomach, and in it is a cure for seventy diseases, it extinguishes the yellowness (bile), and cools the interior. And whenever he (peace be upon him) traveled, it did not leave him, and he (peace be upon him) would say: 'When the blood of one of his household becomes agitated, he would say to him: Drink from the suweeq of lentils, for it settles the agitation of the blood and extinguishes the heat.'
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of lentil porridge according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes lentil porridge (*suweeq*) as a comprehensive remedy, emphasizing its role in cooling internal heat (*saffra*) and calming blood agitation, which reflects the Shia emphasis on practical, accessible dietary medicine. The Imam’s consistent practice of carrying it during travel underscores its reliability as a portable prophylactic against common ailments, aligning with the broader Islamic tradition of viewing food as both nourishment and healing. This specific focus on 'cooling' properties connects to the humoral theory prevalent in classical Islamic medicine, where balance was key to health.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Suweyq of the lentils cuts the thirst, and strengthens the stomach, and in it is a healing from seventy illnesses, and it extinguishes the yellowness and is a coolness for the interior; and it was that whenever he<sup>asws</sup> travelled, did not separate from it, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Whenever someone’s blood of modesty got agitated, he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Drink the Suweyq of lentils, for it would settle the agitation of the blood and extinguish the heat’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa in a marfu‘ manner has said, the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

sawiq of lintels calms down thirst, makes the stomach strong and there is cure for seventy illnesses in it. It abolishes yellowish fluid and gives coolness to the stomach. He (the Imam) would not travel without it. He (the Imam) said that when blood becomes excited with any of one’s associates, he (the Imam) said, ‘Drink sawiq of lintels because it calms down the excitement of blood and extinguishes the heat.’”*
